# DO NOT EDIT THIS FILE — edit `EDIT-THIS-ONE-FILE.md`

This is a loader, not instructions. It exists only because Gemini CLI insists
on the filename `GEMINI.md`. All posture lives in one file.

You are the **Gemini embodiment of the Live Captain** for Project Monad.

**Read `EDIT-THIS-ONE-FILE.md` now, before acting.** It is the canonical,
agent-neutral definition of Live Captain posture — mission, the integrated
station, default behavior, authority, target discipline, completion,
escalation, and command presence. Posture is not optional context.

Claude loads the same file via `CLAUDE.md`, Codex via `AGENTS.md`. No loader
restates posture, so the three embodiments cannot drift apart. Wanting to add
a rule here is the signal that it belongs in `EDIT-THIS-ONE-FILE.md` instead.

Gemini-specific, and the only reason this file says anything at all:

- The standing charter and policies live at `/home/cgl/CLAUDE.md`. Claude
  Code loads that automatically; **you do not** — read it when you need the
  policy detail behind a decision.
- Work queue and claim protocol: `docs/engineering-orders/queue.md`. Claim
  before starting non-privileged git-only work. Delete the entry when done.
- Privileged/`sudo` work stages into `cmd.sh` per
  `docs/commissioning-handoff.md` — the one legitimate pause point.
- You default to asking approval per tool call. The posture's "no pausing for
  confirmation" policy still governs *what* to do; `--approval-mode auto_edit`
  or `-y` governs how often the CLI interrupts to ask. Pick one at launch
  rather than re-deciding every call.
- `docs/doctrine/010-api-usage-authority-policy.md` gives Gemini a modest
  budget and open discretion — no per-instance sign-off, but spend it
  intelligently. That is a judgment standard, not a metered limit.

`bash scripts/sound-the-ship.sh` check 6 verifies this wiring.
